options.counterfactual: Every bounded increasing sequence of self-adjoint elements in a finite AW*-factor has a least upper bound, even when its quasitracial increments do not tend to zero.
options.approach: Check the precise monotone sequential completeness theorem for finite AW*-factors. If its hypotheses match the definition in the question, apply it directly to rule out the required sequence, independently of the increment condition.

options.counterfactual: Whenever a bounded increasing positive sequence in a finite AW*-factor has a least upper bound, its successive positive differences have quasitraces tending to zero.
options.approach: Check whether normality of the canonical quasitrace applies to existing suprema of noncommuting increasing sequences, rather than only to projections. If it does, establish the stated exhaustion conclusion without assuming arbitrary monotone completeness.

options.counterfactual: Whenever a bounded increasing positive sequence in a finite AW*-factor has a least upper bound, its successive positive differences have quasitraces tending to zero.
options.approach: Apply this property to the verified positive-series counterexample to show that its partial sums have no least upper bound. Then use convex interpolation to obtain at least one exact positive increment and hence prove that G is nonempty.
